topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the scope for the lecture series, and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology and the Interplay of Environment, Genetics, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the fundamental biology of cancer development while evaluating the relative contributions of endogenous mutations, chance, genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious pathogens drive cancer development, detailing the biological mechanisms and co-factors involved in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens interact directly or through metabolic activation to cause DNA adducts, damage, and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail non-mutagenic mechanisms of oncogenesis, showing how chronic inflammation, promotional signaling cascades, and host developmental timing permit malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methods used to identify carcinogens and conclude with considerations on evaluating carcinogenic risk.
